explanation: Indonesia is a conservative, Muslim-majority country where public affection beyond hand-holding is generally frowned upon and norms vary sharply by region. In Aceh, the only province enforcing Islamic sharia law, public affection between unmarried couples can be punished with public caning under the local criminal code. Separately, Indonesia's new national Criminal Code (KUHP), in force from January 2, 2026, criminalizes extramarital sex and cohabitation nationwide, though prosecution requires a formal complaint from a spouse, parent, or child — officials have said it is not intended to target tourists.
local_tip: Stick to handshakes, smiles, or at most brief hand-holding in public, and save anything more affectionate for private settings — and be extra cautious in Aceh.
regional_note: In Aceh, public affection between unmarried couples can be punished with public caning (up to around 100 strokes under the Qanun Jinayat) because the province enforces its own sharia-based criminal code.

also_check.note: Casual PDA, including kissing in public, is common and socially accepted.
Public affection between unrelated men and women is prohibited and can carry legal penalties.
PDA is generally avoided in public; even hand-holding is often reserved for more private moments.
